            <h2 class="u-mb-2">UpstreamDrift <span class="u-text-muted">(formerly Golf Modeling Suite)</span></h2>
            <p class="page-lede">
              A unified biomechanical analysis platform consolidating golf swing modeling across multiple physics simulation frameworks. The suite enables comprehensive analysis from simple educational pendulums to complex 290-muscle musculoskeletal models.
            </p>
            <div class="button-row">

          <aside class="site-card site-card--callout u-mb-4">
            <h3 class="u-mb-1">About This Companion Website</h3>
            <p class="resource-description">
              This website serves as a <strong>companion resource</strong> to the Golf Modeling Suite repository. While the repository contains the actual implementation code, simulation models, and technical documentation, this website provides:
            </p>
            <ul class="model-bullet-list">
              <li><strong>Advanced Theory</strong> - Mathematical foundations and control-affine system theory</li>
              <li><strong>Research Context</strong> - Links to academic papers, books, and foundational resources</li>
              <li><strong>Learning Pathways</strong> - Curated educational materials for each physics engine</li>
              <li><strong>Interactive Tools</strong> - Web-based visualizations and calculators</li>
            </ul>
            <p class="resource-description">
              For implementation details, installation instructions, and source code, please visit the <a href="https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift" target="_blank" rel="noopener">GitHub repository</a>.
            </p>

          <!-- Getting Started Section -->
          <div id="getting-started" class="category-section">
            <h3 class="category-title">Getting Started</h3>
          </div>

          <div class="resource-card u-mb-3">
            <h4>Requirements</h4>
            <ul class="model-bullet-list model-bullet-list--leading">
              <li><strong>Python 3.11+</strong> (3.13 recommended)</li>
              <li><strong>Git with LFS support</strong> for large model files</li>
              <li><strong>MATLAB R2023a+</strong> (optional, for Simscape models)</li>
              <li><strong>Conda</strong> optional convenience wrapper for binary dependencies</li>
            </ul>

            <h4 class="u-mt-3">Quick Installation</h4>
            <pre class="code-block"><code>git clone https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift.git
cd UpstreamDrift
git lfs install &amp;&amp; git lfs pull
pip install -e ".[dev]"
python scripts/verify_installation.py</code></pre>
            <p class="resource-description">
              The editable <code>pip install -e ".[dev]"</code> is the canonical install. A conda
              environment (<code>conda env create -f environment.yml &amp;&amp; conda activate upstream-drift</code>)
              is available as a convenience wrapper. For detailed instructions and troubleshooting, see the
              <a href="https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift#installation" target="_blank" rel="noopener">repository documentation</a>.
            </p>
          </div>

          <!-- Application: launcher, web UI, entry points (issues #3337, #3338) -->
          <div class="resource-card u-mb-3">
            <h4>Running the Application</h4>
            <p class="resource-description">
              The recommended entry point launches a FastAPI server (on port 8000) with a
              React/Vite web UI:
            </p>
            <pre class="code-block"><code>python launch_upstream_drift.py            # web UI + API (recommended)
python launch_upstream_drift.py --classic  # classic PyQt6 desktop UI
python launch_upstream_drift.py --api-only # REST API only, no UI
python launch_upstream_drift.py --engine pinocchio  # select an engine</code></pre>
            <p class="resource-description">
              Console scripts <code>upstream-drift</code> and <code>sidekick</code> are also
              installed. For a UI-only exploration without heavy engine dependencies, set
              <code>GOLF_USE_MOCK_ENGINE=1</code>.
            </p>
            <h4 class="u-mt-3">Web UI Pages</h4>
            <p class="resource-description">
              Dashboard, Simulation, Model Explorer, Motion Capture, Analysis Tools,
              Character Builder, Data Explorer, Putting Green, Terrain, and Video Analyzer.
            </p>
            <h4 class="u-mt-3">REST API &amp; Tools</h4>
            <p class="resource-description">
              A REST API (24 routes under <code>src/api/routes/</code>: ball flight, force
              overlays, motion capture, character builder, and more) backs end-user tools in
              <code>src/tools/</code> — ball-flight GUI, swing-flight pipeline, putting-green
              and bunker-shot GUIs, terrain engine, video analyzer, strokes-gained optimizer,
              model explorer, and pose studio — plus motion-capture import (CSV/JSON/C3D with
              OpenPose/MediaPipe retargeting) and an RL/imitation/sim2real learning stack.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div id="physics-engines" class="category-section">
            <h3 class="category-title">Supported Physics Engines</h3>

          <div class="accordion-item">
            <button class="accordion-header" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
              <span>MuJoCo (Recommended)</span>
              <span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true">+</span>
            </button>
            <div class="accordion-content">
              <p class="resource-description">
                <strong>Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact</strong> - The recommended engine for most use cases. MuJoCo provides fast, accurate physics simulation ideal for biomechanical analysis with full musculoskeletal models and contact dynamics.
              </p>
              <h4 class="model-section-h4">Key Capabilities:</h4>
              <ul class="model-bullet-list">
                <li>Full musculoskeletal models with realistic contact</li>
                <li>Model-based optimization and trajectory planning</li>
                <li>Real-time visualization and analysis</li>
                <li>Integration with reinforcement learning frameworks</li>
              </ul>
              <h4>Learning Resources:</h4>
              <ul class="model-bullet-list">
                <li><a href="https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">MuJoCo Documentation</a></li>
                <li><a href="https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/programming.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Programming Guide</a></li>
                <li><a href="https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/discussions" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Community Discussions</a></li>
              </ul>
            </div>

          <div class="accordion-item">
            <button class="accordion-header" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
              <span>Drake</span>
              <span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true">+</span>
            </button>
            <div class="accordion-content">
              <p class="resource-description">
                <strong>MIT Robot Locomotion Group Toolkit</strong> - Specialized for trajectory optimization and model-based design. Drake excels at underactuated systems analysis, making it ideal for studying the control-affine nature of the golf swing.
              </p>
              <h4 class="model-section-h4">Key Capabilities:</h4>
              <ul class="model-bullet-list">
                <li>Trajectory optimization and motion planning</li>
                <li>Underactuated systems analysis</li>
                <li>Control-affine dynamics modeling</li>
                <li>Mathematical program solvers</li>
              </ul>
              <h4>Learning Resources:</h4>
              <ul class="model-bullet-list">
                <li><a href="https://underactuated.mit.edu/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Underactuated Robotics (MIT Course)</a></li>
                <li><a href="https://manipulation.mit.edu/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Robotic Manipulation (MIT Course)</a></li>
                <li><a href="https://drake.mit.edu/pydrake/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">PyDrake API Documentation</a></li>
              </ul>
            </div>
          </div>

          <div class="accordion-item">
            <button class="accordion-header" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
              <span>Pinocchio</span>
              <span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true">+</span>
            </button>
            <div class="accordion-content">
              <p class="resource-description">
                <strong>High-Performance Rigid Body Dynamics</strong> - Based on Roy Featherstone's algorithms, Pinocchio provides efficient computation of forward/inverse dynamics, Jacobians, and constraint handling for multibody systems.
              </p>
              <h4 class="model-section-h4">Key Capabilities:</h4>
              <ul class="model-bullet-list">
                <li>Efficient forward/inverse dynamics</li>
                <li>Analytical Jacobian computation</li>
                <li>Constraint handling for closed-loop mechanisms</li>
                <li>Spatial algebra operations</li>
              </ul>
              <h4>Learning Resources:</h4>
              <ul class="model-bullet-list">
                <li><a href="https://stack-of-tasks.github.io/pinocchio/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Pinocchio Documentation</a></li>
                <li><a href="https://royfeatherstone.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Roy Featherstone's Website</a></li>
                <li><a href="https://www.amazon.com/dp/1447113341" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Rigid Body Dynamics Algorithms (Book)</a></li>
              </ul>
            </div>

              </p>
              <p class="resource-description">
                <strong>Support tier: Experimental.</strong> In UpstreamDrift, OpenSim integration is experimental and is <em>not</em> part of the required PR CI contract today. Treat the musculoskeletal workflow below as exploratory rather than turnkey.
              </p>
              <h4 class="model-section-h4">Key Capabilities:</h4>

            <div class="accordion-content">
              <p class="resource-description">
                <strong>Realistic Muscle Dynamics</strong> - MyoSuite provides 290-muscle musculoskeletal models for detailed muscle-driven movement simulation. Ideal for studying muscle activation patterns and force generation in complex movements.
              </p>
              <p class="resource-description">
                <strong>Support tier: Experimental.</strong> In UpstreamDrift, MyoSuite integration is experimental and is <em>not</em> part of the required PR CI contract today. The 290-muscle workflow is not yet a turnkey, fully-supported pipeline — expect to do setup work.
              </p>
              <h4 class="model-section-h4">Key Capabilities:</h4>
